Fight Costly Violations with a Strategic Traffic Lawyer in Johnson County, IA

Traffic tickets in Johnson County, Iowa, carry real weight. A speeding citation, a reckless driving charge, or a moving violation can add points to your license, raise your insurance rates, and in some cases, put your driving privileges at risk. Henkels & Baker, PC helps drivers across eastern Iowa understand what these charges mean and what options may be available to them.

The courts here handle a high volume of traffic cases each year. Whether your ticket came on Interstate 80, Highway 6, or a local road near Iowa City, the outcome can follow you for years, on your record and in your wallet.

An experienced Johnson County, IA Traffic Lawyer can review the details of your case.

Charges are not always as simple as they appear on the citation. The posted speed limit, road conditions, officer observations, and how the stop was handled all matter.

A thorough review of those facts may reveal options you did not know existed. Henkels & Baker, PC takes a close look at each case before drawing any conclusions about how to move forward.

How Henkels & Baker Handles Traffic Cases in Johnson County

At Henkels & Baker, PC, we start by reviewing the full record of your traffic stop. That means looking at the citation, the officer’s notes, and any court paperwork tied to your case.

Iowa traffic law draws a sharp line between moving and non-moving violations — and that distinction shapes what remedies are available. A charge that looks minor on paper can carry consequences that compound over time, especially for drivers with prior citations.

Your insurance rates can jump after even one moving violation.

We look at what the charge actually says, and whether the stop, the citation, or the charge itself holds up under Iowa law.

Some cases have clear errors. A speed reading from a poorly maintained device, a stop sign that was obscured, or a missed procedural step by the officer — these details matter. We look at every angle to reduce or dismiss your charge.

When dismissal is not the best path, we work toward reduced charges. A moving violation may be negotiable as a non-moving offense. That can protect your license and keep your insurance costs from rising.

Our goal is simple. We work to get you the most favorable outcome your facts allow. We know the Johnson County courts. We know how local prosecutors handle traffic matters. That local knowledge shapes how we build your case from the start.

Common Traffic Penalties

  • Speeding Violations: Fines range from $30 for 1-5 mph over the limit to over $135 plus $5 per additional mph for speeds greater than 20 mph over the limit. Fines double in designated road work zones.

  • Distracted Driving (Hands-Free Law): Holding or manually using a cell phone while driving is illegal in Iowa (Iowa Code 321.276). A standard violation results in a $100 fine. Fines escalate to $500 if it results in injury, and 1,000 if it causes death.

  • Reckless Driving: Classed as a simple misdemeanor, carrying up to 30 days in jail and fines between $105 and $625.

  • OWI (Operating While Intoxicated): A first offense is a serious misdemeanor carrying a maximum of 1 year in jail, fines of $625 to $1,250, and an automatic license revocation.

  • Hit and Run (Leaving the Scene): Penalties scale depending on damage and injury severity, ranging from a simple misdemeanor (up to 30 days in jail) to a Class D felony for fatal accidents (up to 5 years in prison).

  • Serious Injury or Death: Causing serious injury due to a traffic violation can result in a $500 fine or 90-day license suspension. Causing death can lead to a $1,000 fine or a 180-day license suspension.

You get a direct conversation before you commit to anything. Henkels & Baker, PC, offers free consultations where you can ask straightforward questions about your Johnson County traffic case and your options.

No vague answers. No sales pitch.

Henkels & Baker, PC, knows the courts and procedures across this region well.

Larger firms often divide attention across many clients at once. At Henkels & Baker, PC, you get personal attention. Your case gets time and care. That shows in every step of the process.

Your Traffic Case in Johnson County, Iowa: Step by Step

Traffic cases in Johnson County move through a clear process. Knowing what comes next helps you stay calm and make smart choices.

Stage 1: Citation and Response Deadline (Days 1–30)

You receive a traffic citation. It lists a court date or a deadline to respond. In Iowa, most simple traffic violations require a written plea or an in-person appearance within 30 days. Missing this window can lead to a default judgment or a suspended license.

As your lawyer, we can review the citation, check for errors, and advise you on your plea options before that deadline hits.

Stage 2: Initial Court Appearance (Week 2–4)

Your first appearance is typically at the Johnson County Courthouse in Iowa City. You enter a plea: not guilty, guilty, or no contest. We may waive this appearance on your behalf for minor violations under Iowa Code Chapter 805.

The goal at this stage is to keep your options open and buy time to build your case.

Stage 3: Case Review and Negotiation (Weeks 2–6)

This is where real work happens. Your lawyer pulls the police report, reviews the officer’s notes, and looks for issues with how the stop or citation was handled. Many Johnson County traffic cases settle at this stage through a plea deal — sometimes reducing charges or swapping a moving violation for a non-moving one to protect your driving record.

Stage 4: Pre-Trial Motions (If Needed)

If there are legal grounds to challenge the stop or the evidence, your lawyer may file motions before trial.

In Iowa, a motion to suppress can ask the court to throw out evidence gathered in an unlawful stop. The Johnson County District Court handles these hearings.

Stage 5: Trial or Final Resolution

Most traffic cases resolve before trial. If yours does go to a hearing, it takes place in Iowa City before a judge; there is no jury for simple traffic violations in Iowa. Here we can present your defense, cross-examine the officer, and argue for dismissal or reduction.

A final ruling typically comes the same day.

Talk to a Traffic Lawyer in Johnson County Today

A traffic citation in Johnson County can affect your license, your insurance, and your job. Don’t wait to get help. At Henkels & Baker, PC, we offer free consultations. You can ask real questions and get honest answers — no pressure, no commitment.

Ready to move forward? Here are your next steps. Contact us to schedule your initial consultation and talk through your options. Tell us what happened — we’ll review the facts and explain what we can do.

The sooner you call, the more we can do to help protect your record and your license.

Frequently Asked Questions

1. Can I just pay my traffic ticket and skip court in Johnson County?

Paying a ticket is treated as a guilty plea in Iowa, which means points go on your record, and your insurance rates may rise. An experienced traffic lawyer may be able to negotiate a reduced charge or a dismissal before you pay anything.

2. Will a speeding ticket affect my commercial driver’s license?

CDL holders face stricter rules under federal regulations — even a minor speeding violation can trigger disqualification thresholds that don’t apply to standard licenses. If you hold a CDL, the stakes of any traffic charge in Iowa are much higher than a typical ticket.

3. How long do I have to respond to a traffic citation in Iowa?

Iowa traffic citations typically require a response or appearance within the number of days listed on the citation, and missing that deadline can result in a license suspension. Acting quickly gives your lawyer the best chance to explore your options before the window closes.

4. What if I was ticketed in Johnson County, but I live out of state?

Out-of-state drivers are still subject to Iowa traffic law, and a conviction may transfer to your home state under the Driver License Compact agreement.

5. Can traffic violations from Johnson County be expunged from my Iowa record?

Iowa law allows expungement of certain criminal records, but most traffic violations are civil infractions and are subject to different rules. Talking to a lawyer about your specific citation type is the best way to understand what relief, if any, may be available.
